title: Credibility Assessment of Implicit FEA Models for Bone Screw Thread Insertion Torque Under Four Mechanisms
device: Orthopedic cortical bone screw with self-tapping thread

models.name: Axisymmetric Equivalent-Thread Model (AETM)
models.what_it_computes: Homogenized thread–bone contact response to estimate insertion torque versus depth using axisymmetric implicit FEA with Coulomb friction and ploughing resistance.

models.name: 3D Half-Turn Helical Segment (HTHS)
models.what_it_computes: Non-axisymmetric torque from a half-turn of helical thread with detailed flank geometry using implicit contact; chip formation is represented by a viscoplastic cutting surrogate to capture torque spikes.

models.name: Multi-Scale Cortical–Cancellous Coupled Model (MS-CCC)
models.what_it_computes: Torque contributions from cortical and cancellous regions via a macroscale screw–bone model coupled to an orthotropic damage RVE; solved implicitly with a user material subroutine.

mechanisms.name: Frictional and Ploughing Interface
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Thread–bone tangential resistance dominates steady-state torque; mis-specified friction or embedment leads to biased torque predictions.

mechanisms.name: Pilot Hole and Cortex Tolerance
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Variation in pilot diameter and cortical thickness changes interference and contact pressure, shifting torque–depth curves.

mechanisms.name: Self-Tapping and Chip Formation
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Cutting and chip evacuation introduce transient peaks and added resistance that affect maximum torque and risk of thread stripping.

mechanisms.name: Bone Microstructure and Damage Evolution
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Anisotropy, porosity, and damage softening alter local shear strength, modifying torque escalation and relaxation with advancing depth.

deviation.detail: All factor scores are reported on a private 0–7 Credibility Units scale with defined anchors for each factor; per-pair scores are compiled for every model–mechanism combination.

sections: Device and Measured Quantity: Self-Tapping Bone Screw Insertion Torque
Computational Models: Geometry, Material Laws, Contact, and Solution Controls
Data Pedigree for Material, Contact, and Geometric Inputs
Model Inputs and Equivalency of Input Parameters Across Models and Tests
Model Form Evaluation for Each Mechanism
Numerical Code Verification for Implicit Contact and Nonlinear Material Response
Numerical Solver Error: Convergence Metrics, Step Control, and Mesh Refinement
Test Samples: Specimen Types, Manufacturing Tolerances, and Measurement Methods
Output Comparison: Torque–Depth and Peak Torque Versus Mechanism-Specific Benchmarks
Software Quality Assurance and Use History (summary notes)
Per-Pair Factor Scoring Matrix (private 0–7 scale) and Thresholds
Discussion of Cross-Mechanism Consistency and Residual Gaps

Conclusion—The model suite is not accepted for predicting insertion torque of this bone screw because output comparisons under the Self-Tapping and Chip Formation mechanism failed to meet comparison criteria, and friction/damage input pedigree was insufficient to support the reported scores; additional verified formulation and higher-grade test evidence are required.
